sysd-reliab-083.caption: Each technique keeps a spare or independent component ready in a different way.
header: How it keeps the service up
rows: Identical instances run in parallel; quorum picks the result
Identical instances; switch to a remaining one on failure
Different implementations of the same specification
Traffic spread so no server is a single point of failure

sysd-reliab-176.caption: One absolute deadline shrinks as each call spends time, so every later call knows how long is left.
bars: Deadline set high in the stack
Left for the call after that

sysd-reliab-088.caption: Tokens arrive at a fixed rate, and a packet is sent only if the bucket holds enough of them.
sysd-reliab-088.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Token every 1/r seconds] --> B[(Bucket: at most b tokens)]
B --> C{n tokens available?}
C -->|yes| D[Remove n tokens, send packet]
C -->|no| E[Non-conformant: queue or mark]

sysd-reliab-076.caption: The five algorithms differ in what they keep and when they discard a request.
rows: First-in, first-out queue; discards when full
Each request takes a token; none left, refused
Counter per window of n seconds; discards above a threshold
Time-stamped log per request; sums logs for the rate
Hybrid: adds a weighted previous window

sysd-reliab-069.caption: Read each row to compare how long a client waits and where the strategy falls short.
rows: Grows exponentially: 1, 2, 4, 8 seconds, up to a maximum
Can delay a fix a quick retry would reach
Large jitter delays more than needed

sysd-reliab-073.caption: The server's lookup of the key decides whether the request is processed or answered from the saved response.
sysd-reliab-073.mermaid:
flowchart TD
A[Client sends request with key] --> B{Key already stored?}
B -->|no| C[Store key, process request]
C --> D[Save response against key]
B -->|yes| E[Skip processing]
E --> F[Return saved response]

sysd-reliab-068.caption: Read each row to see whether calls reach the service in that state and what moves the breaker on.
rows: Failures rise beyond the threshold: open
They succeed: closed; they keep failing: open
